subject: Hosted eval: quickstart path, endpoints & rate limits — ops summary
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khouri <samira@checkout.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted eval: quickstart path, endpoints & rate limits — post-demo follow-up

Hi Samira —

Great demo yesterday — thanks for taking the time. Quick recap and the immediate asks we discussed so we have alignment on the fast path for a hosted evaluation: 

- Scope: API text generation (customer support summarization + search rerank). No embeddings for initial pilot.
- Success criteria: 95th pct latency < 350ms on 512-token prompt, throughput to support 10 TPS sustained with bursts to 50 TPS during peak.
- Security: standard SOC2+VPC peering later if we move to Dedicated/Private, but initial hosted is fine per your security team for non-PII workloads.

Concrete next steps (owner in parentheses):
1) I will provision sandbox endpoints and share keys (Ben) — expected by EOD tomorrow.
2) You to confirm representative traffic profile and a 1-hour sample corpus for eval (Samira/Diego).
3) Ops question: do you want a single endpoint (mixed-size) or separate endpoints tuned for short/long responses? (Samira)
4) Rate guidance: hosted trial supports 10 TPS by default; we can extend to 30 TPS for short pilot with a temporary uplift — tell me your target.

I attached a quickstart checklist and the recording from yesterday. I kept the checklist minimal so your engineers can run the smoke tests in <24 hours.

If you prefer a Dedicated-capacity conversation, we can scope that in parallel — it will add a short procurement step but gives you isolation and higher predictable throughput. For now, hosted is the fastest onramp.

Thanks — I’ll send the sandbox keys tomorrow once I confirm the routing map with infra.

Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-quickstart-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Samira Khouri <samira@checkout.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Alvarez <diego@checkout.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted eval: quickstart path, endpoints & rate limits — post-demo follow-up

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Traffic profile: mostly short prompts (~64 tokens) for real-time summarization, but ~20% of requests are long (350–700 tokens) for full-context extracts. Peak TPS target is 40 TPS; sustained target 12 TPS.
- We’ll share a one-hour sample capture (anonymized) by EOD today. Diego will attach the sample.
- Regarding endpoints: we prefer two endpoints to keep short-request latency optimized and avoid KV cache thrash for long requests.

Quick Q on rate uplift: can you confirm if the temporary uplift to 30 TPS you mentioned applies per endpoint or per API key? We’d likely need the uplift per endpoint.

Samira
Head of Integrations | Checkout.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khouri <samira@checkout.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Diego Alvarez <diego@checkout.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted eval: quickstart path, endpoints & rate limits — post-demo follow-up

Samira — thanks, that profile helps. Short answers below and an ops plan: 

- Uplift semantics: temporary uplift is configured per endpoint. For hosted trials we can set short-endpoint to 50 TPS burst / 30 TPS sustained, long-endpoint to 10 TPS sustained. If you need higher sustained on the short endpoint we’ll need a short commercial uplift (one-page MSA amendment) but we can paper that quickly.

- Endpoint plan (Ops):
  * short-api.checkout.redwood/v1/generate — tuned runtime with aggressive batching and smaller max-seq (optimized kernels)
  * long-api.checkout.redwood/v1/generate — KV-aware runner, larger sequence budget, separate KV caches

- Keys & sandboxes: I’ll issue two sandbox API keys scoped to each endpoint. Keys will be rate-limited and logged separately so you can map cost/latency.

- Monitoring: we’ll provide a temporary Dashboard link (retention 7d) with per-key latency percentiles and token breakdown. After the pilot we can extend retention and hook into your Datadog via metrics bridge.

Next operational asks for your eng team (Diego):
1) Confirm desired burst and sustained TPS per endpoint (short / long) — reply inline.
2) Confirm sample corpus uploaded to the Drive link (Samira) — I’ll validate and provision routes once it’s there.
3) If you want VPC peering for logs/metrics now, flag it; otherwise we’ll defer to Dedicated conversation.

I attached the checklist again with a short ops runbook callout. I’ll start provisioning keys as soon as you confirm rates.

Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-quickstart-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: quick ops alignment for Checkout.ai hosted trial

Ben / Monica — internal note before we send the uplift paperwork: 

- If they request short-endpoint sustained >30 TPS we should prepare a one-page uplift (legal-friendly, no new MSA) and estimate incremental monthly committed spend. Finance prefers we target $6k–12k/month for sustained 30–60 TPS depending on token mix.
- Ops: Monica please pre-provision the short/long endpoint runners with labels and a dedicated KV cache for the long runner. Use quantization profile Q3 for short-runner to keep latency down.
- CS: Ben, coordinate with Marissa for success criteria instrumentation and the 95th percentile SLA note in the pilot plan.

I’ll stand by to approve the uplift form once Ben sends the customer-confirmed numbers.

Jordan Blake
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
